title: A Semester for the Prom
premise: Vesper Okafor has perfected the art of disappearing: ace debater, invisible daughter, senior counting down to graduation. When her best friend Priya vanishes, leaving only her car keys and a half-finished college application, Vesper is forced into the spotlight she's spent years avoiding. Following Priya's trail through a championship debate season, Vesper uncovers that her friend fled an abusive home — and that staying silent made her complicit. In the end, Vesper wins the state final by abandoning her prepared case to tell the truth about what happened, then drives to find Priya, choosing loyalty over the safe future she'd been serving time for.
about_author: Coral Pemberton is a former high-school debate coach who spent six years watching teenagers argue beautifully about things they couldn't say at home. She writes from a small coastal town where she keeps a drawer full of confiscated tournament notes.

chapters.title: Ninety-Three Days
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Opening on a debate practice she dominates effortlessly, then home, where she loses every argument with her controlling father without raising her voice. Establishes her countdown calendar and her survival strategy of invisibility. Emotional beat: quiet resignation disguised as control.

chapters.title: The Keys
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Priya misses their traditional Friday diner ritual — unheard of in eight years of friendship. At Priya's house, Vesper finds the car keys left deliberately on the porch rail, no note, bedroom stripped of anything personal. Emotional beat: dread cracking open routine.

chapters.title: Missing Persons
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Vesper and Detective Ruiz. The police are polite but unconvinced; Priya is seventeen, 'likely a runaway.' Vesper insists Priya would never leave without telling her, but can't explain why she's so certain. Emotional beat: the humiliation of not being believed.

chapters.title: What Everyone Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She interviews classmates using debate techniques — cross-examination as investigation. Fragments emerge: Priya crying in the bathroom after a phone call, a bruise explained away, a boy named Theo who saw her near the bus station. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Case Nobody Argues
chapters.summary: Coach Danvers' POV. Tournament season begins; the team needs Vesper focused. He notices her distraction but recognizes something familiar in it — his own sister ran away decades ago. He gives her a gruff ultimatum wrapped in unexpected kindness. Emotional beat: reluctant mentorship.

chapters.title: Priya's Locker
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. With Theo's help, Vesper opens Priya's untouched locker: a burner phone, cash, and a printed bus schedule circled for the night she vanished. Priya planned this — but the phone holds one saved contact labeled only 'HELP.' Emotional beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Home Court
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Her father discovers the missing-person flyers in her backpack and forbids her involvement, threatening to pull her from debate season entirely. A screaming match where Vesper finally raises her voice — and immediately regrets how good it feels. Emotional beat: first open rebellion.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo reveals he and Priya were secretly dating; her parents hated him. He shows Vesper texts where Priya hinted her father's temper was escalating. Vesper confronts the possibility she ignored signs to protect her own fragile peace. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Prelims
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. First tournament: Vesper debates flawlessly on autopilot while mentally drafting a map of everywhere Priya might have gone. She qualifies for regionals but realizes winning feels like nothing now. Emotional beat: hollow victory, recalibrated priorities.

chapters.title: The Burner Rings
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The HELP number calls the burner — a women's shelter intake line two states away. They won't confirm residents, but a volunteer mentions a girl who asked about job training programs. Vesper now knows Priya chose to leave, and chose safety over goodbye. Emotional beat: relief tangled with hurt.

chapters.title: Two Truths
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper tells her mother everything. Her mother's reaction — fear, then a whispered admission about her own marriage — reframes the household: her father's control isn't new, just unchallenged. Emotional beat: generational pattern exposed.

chapters.title: Regionals
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At regionals, Vesper faces rival debater Camille Zhao, who dismantles her rehearsed case. Losing stings less than expected; losing teaches her that prepared arguments are armor, not truth. She advances anyway on points. Emotional beat: humility as fuel.

chapters.title: The Father's Version
chapters.summary: Priya's father's POV (brief, unsettling). He performs grief publicly while privately burning Priya's belongings. Through him, readers glimpse what Priya fled — and why she couldn't trust anyone to believe her. Emotional beat: chilling confirmation.

chapters.title: Runaway Logic
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper reconstructs Priya's planning like a debate case: money saved, route chosen, shelter researched. The conclusion devastates her — Priya trusted no one, including Vesper, because Vesper had once dismissed a cry for help. Emotional beat: reckoning with complicity.

chapters.title: Semifinal Week
chapters.summary: Coach Danvers' POV. State semifinals approach; Vesper is distracted, brilliant, and unraveling. Danvers offers her a choice: drop out and go find her friend, or stay and finish what they started. She chooses both, and he quietly arranges travel that overlaps with the tournament city. Emotional beat: alliance formed.

chapters.title: The City Where She Went
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Between rounds, Vesper searches the shelter neighborhood, leaving notes in places Priya might pass. A near-miss: someone matching Priya's description watches her from across the street and walks away. Emotional beat: agonizing proximity.

chapters.title: State Final
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The championship round: Vesper abandons her prepared affirmative case mid-speech to argue, raw and true, about the price of silence — using Priya's story anonymized but unmistakable. She wins on a split decision and doesn't care. Emotional beat: identity claimed.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The speech goes viral locally; Priya's father threatens legal action; Vesper's father demands she recant. Instead, standing in the kitchen, Vesper tells him plainly what she saw growing up and that she will not inherit his silence. Emotional beat: the argument at home finally won.

chapters.title: A Letter Forwarded Twice
chapters.summary: Priya's POV (first appearance). From the shelter, Priya reads about the speech online and writes to Vesper care of the school — not forgiveness yet, but acknowledgment: 'You said it out loud. That counts.' Emotional beat: tentative bridge.

chapters.title: Spring Break
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper takes the bus to the shelter town with her mother's blessing and her own savings. She waits outside for three days before Priya appears — thinner, wary, alive. No speeches; they sit on a bench until the wariness thaws. Emotional beat: earned reunion.

chapters.title: What Winning Means
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Graduation day. Vesper declines the ceremonial spotlight to introduce Priya, back enrolled in a district program, from the audience instead. Her father attends but stays seated; her mother stands and applauds. Emotional beat: belonging redefined on her own terms.

chapters.title: Day One
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue tone. Summer begins: no countdown calendar, just a blank notebook and a plan to study law. Final image — Vesper and Priya driving nowhere in particular with the windows down, keys in the ignition this time. Emotional beat: survival transformed into beginning.
